授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（英語）:
This course offers an overview of the key characteristics and main issues of contemporary Japanese society from an international perspective. It is primarily designed for international undergraduate students who are new to the study of Japanese society, but it also welcomes Japanese students who wish to deepen, update, or reshape their understanding of these topics through a cross-national and critical lens. Graduate students are encouraged to join too, as long as they are aware of the course's entry-level content.
As an introductory sociology course, this course will address various features and socio-cultural issues in contemporary Japan. Topics will include, but are not limited to, social stratification (class and inequalities), gender inequalities, race and ethnic relations, intergenerational relations, age-related social norms, education, religion, popular culture, politics, and family dynamics. Students will explore these subjects through formal lectures, in-class discussions, take-home assignments, and supplemental readings.
授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.履修条件:
No prerequisite (please see below, however).
This is an all-English course designed originally for international/exchange students. Domestic students, including Japanese students, are more than welcome to join, and it’s not required possess a certain level of proficiency in English to formally enroll in this course. However, if you are not a native English speaker, it’s important to possess a minimum level of English skills necessary to meaningfully participate in and successfully complete this course. This course advises that you possess a minimum TOEFL score of 79 (IBT) or IELTS 6.0.
